newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NAMIBIA CABINET POSTPONES DECISION ON SAB.
newsitem.headline: NAMIBIA CABINET POSTPONES DECISION ON SAB.

text.p: The Namibian cabinet did not reach a decision on an application by South African Breweries to set up a N$100 million ($21 million) brewery at Oshakati in northern Namibia.
The ministers did not say when a decision, which was expected on Wednesday, would be made.
Despite the offer of 51 percent of the shares to local businessmen, a step towards black economic empowerment in Namibia, a thumbs-up for the venture seems unlikely.
Trade and Industry Minister Hidipo Hamutenya told reporters on Tuesday that as far as he was concerned the government's position on the matter had not changed.

A first proposal by SAB in 1995 for a bottling plant at Tsumeb was turned down after the Namibia Breweries Limited (NBL) objected, saying an SAB plant in Namibia would destroy the local company's market because the country was too small to entertain Hamutenya told a local newspaper that the government would not support any foreign monopoly at the expense of a local competitor.
"We have a company that is Namibian, that pays tax, and is the largest manufacturing plant, employing over 700 Namibians," he was quoted as saying.
"We cannot let it be overrun by SAB, as has been the case in other African countries where SAB has set up breweries."
SAB dominates the Southern African market with Namibia Breweries its only competitor.
If it succeeds in its application, the brewery will supply the northern Namibian and southern Angolan market with up to 300,000 hectolitres of beer a year.
Namibia Breweries' seven beers are sold in South Africa, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Angola at premium market prices.
In the 1996 financial year NBL reported record sales of over 700,000 hectolitres for the first time.
